subject: Dedicated capacity — proposed amendment to queue behavior and throughput safety net
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

David — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our infra lead dug into the traffic patterns and we have one ask before we can finalize the commitment: during our nightly batch window (02:00–05:00 local), we run large bulk scoring jobs that spike concurrent inflight tokens and are sensitive to preemption.

Specifically: we need an amendment that limits preemption of our reserved GPUs during the nightly window and guarantees a minimal throughput floor (measured as tokens/s per reservation) to avoid long tail latency regressions for those batch jobs.

We put a short draft amendment on Drive (link below) and attached our last 30 days of usage for reference. Two quick questions up front:
- Is Redwood open to a time-boxed carveout (nightly 3h window) with a soft headroom credit if preemption occurs?
- If we accept a modest monthly premium, can you commit to a 95th-percentile throughput floor for inflight batch jobs (we can provide a short eval prompt set to verify)?

Attaching draft and stats. Happy to discuss with product/ops/legal.

Thanks,
Alex
Ops Lead, Hedgewell Technologies
attachments: hedgewell-draft-amendment.pdf (application/pdf), hedgewell-usage-stats.csv (text/csv)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

Alex — appreciate the detail and the files. Looping in Marissa (Product, Dedicated Capacity) and Laura (Legal) so we can get a cross-functional view. Quick read: your ask breaks into two parts (operational carveout for nightly window + throughput floor).

Here's how we typically handle similar asks:
- Nightly time-boxed carveouts: possible as a limited addendum. We can reduce preemption over that window by reserving a small percentage of the pool for your tenancy, or configuring a soft-preempt threshold.
- Throughput floor (tokens/s guarantee): harder at 95th percentile without additional margin — it depends on model, sequence length, and KV-cache hit rate. We can propose a measurable SLO tied to specific model variants and prompt sets.

Marissa — can you review the attached usage and advise what measurable floor we could realistically propose for a 3-hour nightly window on the r-large family? Also, what premium would procurement expect for a soft headroom reservation (e.g., additional reserved GPUs vs. commitment fee)?

Laura — if we agree to a carveout/credit approach, what contractual language should we propose to limit exposure (time-boxed, revocation with notice, caps on crediting)?

Alex — propose a short call tomorrow to walk through our proposal and the metrics you'll use for validation.

Best,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: (555) 212-3344

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

Thanks David. Alex — quick read of your CSV suggests your nightly jobs are heavy on long-context scoring (avg seq len ~1024) with KP cache miss rate ~18%. That makes a hard 95th token/s guarantee expensive unless we raise reserved capacity or accept stricter preemption control.

Proposal (initial):
- Nightly window 02:00–05:00 PT: create a "soft-safety lane" that pins 8 GPUs (r-large equivalent) to Hedgewell's pool. These are billed as reserved for the window; outside the window they are part of the normal pool.
- If preemption occurs inside the window (rare, emergency maintenance), Hedgewell receives credits equal to 2x average token cost for the affected window (applied to next invoice).
- Measurable SLO: 99th-percentile tail latency for batch jobs during window <= 2.1s per batch token for provided eval set (we'll run validation on your prompt set).

Premium estimate: roughly a 12% uplift on monthly dedicated commit for the "pinned 8 GPUs" approach vs. a lower-commit soft-reserve. If Hedgewell wants no billing delta, then we'd need to accept a broader preemption allowance and a looser SLO.

If that sounds in the ballpark, I'll draft the amendment language and the test harness. David — want to run pricing with Sales Ops and send a skeleton term sheet?

Marissa
Director, Product — Dedicated Capacity

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hedgewell.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

Marissa — thanks, that proposal is actionable and very close to what we discussed internally. A few clarifications:
- The 8 GPU pin during the window should be sufficient for the first phase. We may scale to 12 during Q4, but can commit to 8 for the initial 6 months.
- Credits: please confirm the mechanics (how credits are calculated and applied). The twofold token-cost credit seems reasonable as a deterrent to preemption, but procurement asks for a cap (e.g., total credits in a month not to exceed 20% of monthly committed spend).
- Validation: we can share a 1000-sample prompt set for your test harness. Can you confirm timeline to run validation and share results?

Procurement looped in for pricing/contract language. Happy to take a short call tomorrow at 11:00 PT.

—Alex

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

Alex — quick note on contract language controls:
- Limit the carveout to an initial 6-month term with automatic review; include a clause that allows Redwood to reclaim the daily pins for emergency maintenance with 72 hours' notice.
- Cap monthly credits as you requested (suggested cap: 20% of committed monthly spend, but Sales Ops must confirm numeric mapping).
- Define validation harness pass/fail criteria clearly and bind them to a one-time acceptance window (we can schedule an acceptance run and record token-level metrics).

I'll circulate a short amendment template with redlines after Sales Ops confirms the premium.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@hedgewell.com>, procurement@hedgewell.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated pool queue behavior amendment (Hedgewell)

Alex / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Next steps:
1) Marissa will run a validation pass on your 1k sample set and share results by EOD Monday.
2) Sales Ops will produce a term sheet with the 12% premium estimate and the alternative soft-reserve pricing.
3) Laura will draft the amendment with the 6-month initial term, 72-hour emergency reclaim clause, and the 20% credit cap.
4) We'll hold the call tomorrow 11:00 PT to align on acceptance criteria and timeline; invite sent.

If these steps work, we'll prepare an interim MOU for signatures so procurement can start internal approval.

Best,
David
attachments: none
